rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a supplementary reading (maintainer block, lines 149-153: 'Reading material for AE101 M6 practitioner-mode beat... Optional reading after M6 closes'), not an in-room teaching beat, so mood-floor scoring is exempt per §1's setup/teaching diagnostic — but the file still frames rather than resolves M6's mood. M6's deliberate mood is 'practitioner fluency — I know how to test, I know how to learn, I know how to encode' (strategy doc line ~475/480). The file's own close (lines 133-143, 'How to pick what to study') hands the student three filters instead of a verdict — 'Two or three practitioners is enough to track... The composition conversation will keep moving' — which is judgment-driven, matching practitioner-fluency, not a lecture that resolves the question for the student.

Closest-to-violating line is 95: 'Composition fluency erodes the review discipline that originally justified composition' (Willison's normalization-of-deviance framing inside the Ronacher counter-section) — this reads as a systemic/field-level warning, not a personal-failure charge at the student. No 'you messed up' framing anywhere; the Ronacher section (89-101) is posed as an open question ('what is your review bandwidth?') the student answers, not a verdict on something the student already did wrong.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All seven section headers name a practitioner + a discipline/shape, not a failure word: 'Compound Engineering', 'Composition by invocation', 'Single writer with advisor agents', 'Feedback-loopable methodology and shipped primitives', 'Practitioner moves without a published framework', 'Counter-position, Armin Ronacher', 'Skill stacking system, Dino: the worked example'. The Ronacher section argues a counter-position (review bandwidth as the constraint) but is titled by its stance, not by a failure noun ('review debt' appears in body prose only, never as a heading).

Strategy doc M6-in-detail (lines 447-491) states the second-authored-skill build was cut from in-module work and now lands as a post-module handoff prompt, and that scheduled agents are 'a callout, not an exercise' that 'lands naturally post-training or in a followup module.' This supplementary does not smuggle either back in — it contains no skill-authoring exercise and no scheduled-agent instruction; it is pure reading material delivered after M6 closes (maintainer block lines 149-153: 'Linked from M6's composing-the-workflow.md lecture. Optional reading after M6 closes, or pre-read between M6 and post-cohort follow-up'), so it sits after the M6 teaching moment it pairs with rather than front-running it. One process note for the maintainer, not a rule violation: the strategy doc's own 'Supplementary material — Shipped' list (lines 777-786) enumerates agentic-engineering-progression.md, clean-code-is-steering.md, verification-asymmetry.md, and how-the-best-do-ci-cd.md as shipped, but does not list workflow-composition-lineages.md — the canon doc appears not to have been updated when this supplementary shipped. This is a doc-hygiene gap, not a content drift inside the file under review, so it is not scored as a strategy-fidelity REVISE against this file.
